The description of these filters gives the impression they are certified as NSF 42 and 53 filters. They are not. I became suspicious because there are no claims to that effect on the box or filter (though they include meaningless fine print to make it look like they might be), so I came back and looked at the description, and looked at their Web site (...), and then checked the NSF site. They also look cheaply made compared to other filters I have purchased, cheap plastic and big seams. Now I feel like I've been taken. If you just want a cheap filter that is compatible with a UKF8001, then this does the trick. But who knows if it's actually filtering your water. It's not certified to meet any standards!

I rarely write reviews, but this is the best kitchen gadget I've gotten in a long time. I love to chew on crushed ice all day - helps increase my water intake, and I've loved crushed ice since I was a kid. The ice dispenser on our old fridge died, so I was searching for something to use until we get a new one. Tripped over this, and read a lot of reviews, and was helped greatly by a few people who mentioned the consistency/texture of this ice.
Prior to this, the best ice I had ever come across to crunch on was the ice you get at the hospital (not familiar with the Sonic restaurant ice several people mentioned), but this is even better to me. The cubes are essentially like little, hollow bullets. I always pick the "small" size (can make either small or large ones) - I assume the large ones are just maybe thicker. But the texture is almost like compressed shaved ice. Perfect for ice chewers, as it still has the crunch, but is not hard on teeth or dental work at all. It's a little harder when it first comes out (but even then I think it still wouldn't harm teeth), but as it sits for a few minutes, it becomes even more awesome.
It is super easy to use and makes ice pretty quickly, too. I fill it up with approx. 9 cups of water in the morning, and then just add water periodically during the day. It makes around 10 cubes each cycle, but it makes them every few minutes and they build up fast. It is also very easy to clean/maintain. At the end of the day

I live in Las Vegas and drink ice water all day long. I got sick of fighting with ice cube trays. Ice doesn't come out of plastic trays, and the modern version of the metal trays our parents used are so flimsy that they break more easily than the ice they contain. I also got sick of ice in my freezer all solidifying into one massive lump. This ice maker is the perfect answer. I just leave it running around the clock. No, it doesn't keep ice frozen, but when the ice melts, the water goes back in the reservoir and is reprocessed. Several times every day, I go to my machine, and there is always ice waiting without struggling with trays or having to chisel cubes apart. If your kitchen isn't set up to allow a fridge with an ice-maker, this is definitely the next-best option. Of course, with Amazon, you know you're going to get the best, fastest delivery possible.

When I ordered this, my only intention was to use it when traveling in our fifth wheel.  However, it worked so well on the road, that we decided to bring it back into the kitchen with us when we returned home.  I haven't had to pop a plastic ice tray since!  I simply refill it each evening and let it make ice for a few hours before bedtime.  The first batch or two is rather wet and soft; but, once it gets going it gets much more efficient.  Produces nice round cubes and lots of them in a short amount of time. I usually empty into a large bin in the freezer after each couple of dumps because the ice in the basket does melt rather quickly.  Be sure to give the unit plenty of room for ventilation since it does generate a bit of warm air while running. And sit back and enjoy having ice without popping trays!

The overall machine is simple and straightforward, makes excellent ice, and is compact and sleek looking.
